name: Sovereign BRRRR Command Center
tag: Model buy, rehab, rent, refinance and repeat deals with clear numbers and stress tests.

scenarios.title: Run the numbers on one deal
scenarios.ask: Buy at ${price}, rehab for ${rehab}, after-repair value ${arv}, rent ${rent} a month. How much cash stays in the deal?
steps: All-in cost: ${=price + rehab} plus a sample ${=round((price + rehab) * 0.04)} in closing and holding costs.
Cash-out refinance at 75% of after-repair value: ${=round(arv * 0.75)} loan.
Sample 30-year loan at 7.5%: about ${=round(arv * 0.75 * 0.007)} a month.
Rent minus the loan payment and 40% for taxes, insurance, repairs, vacancy and management.

result.title: Deal summary
rows: Illustration with sample rates; not financial advice

followups: It is a common planning rule for taxes, insurance, repairs, vacancy and management. You can replace it with real numbers for each line.
Getting most of your cash back at refinance. When cash left in the deal is near zero, that money can fund the next purchase.

scenarios.title: Stress test a rental
scenarios.ask: My rental refinanced at ${loan}. What if rates rise {bump} points at the next refi and vacancy hits {vacancy}?
steps: At 7.5%, payment is about ${=round(loan * 0.007)} a month.
At {=7.5 + bump}%, payment rises to about ${=round(loan * (0.007 + bump * 0.0007))}.
Compared cash flow before and after both shocks.
followups: How do I protect against this?
Common steps are a cash reserve of 6 months of payments, about ${=round(loan * 0.007 * 6)} here, and a fixed-rate loan when possible.
It is a close estimate for a 30-year fixed loan. The full model uses exact amortization and your actual tax and insurance bills.

scenarios.title: Plan the next 12 months
scenarios.ask: I start with ${cash} cash and want to complete deals of about ${allin} all-in, recovering {recover} at refi.
steps: Assumed a sample short-term loan covering 80% of each deal, so each deal needs ${=round(allin * 0.2)} down.
{recover} of your cash comes back about 6 months after each purchase.
Laid out purchases across 12 months so cash is never below zero.
Flagged the month where reserves are lowest.

result.title: 12-month plan
rows: Deals you can start at once
Illustration; timelines and lender terms vary

followups: What if I can't start any deals?
If cash per deal is above your starting cash, the plan suggests a partner, a smaller deal size or a lender with lower down payment.
Why does recovery matter so much?
Each point of recovery is cash you can reuse. At {recover}, most of your money goes back to work after each refinance.
